newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway signs 25 year Italy gas supply deal.
newsitem.headline: Norway signs 25 year Italy gas supply deal.

text.p: Norway's gas negotiating committee (GFU) has signed a deal with Italian gas company SNAM SpA, a subsidiary of ENI SpA, to deliver six billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas per year, state company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Tuesday.
At current prices, the overall value of the contract is about 90 billion crowns, Statoil said in a statement.
The statement said deliveries would begin in the year 2000 and reach plateau level in 2002.
Running for 25 years, the contract is one of the largest in Norway's gas history and the first sale of Norwegian gas to Italy.
A total of 150 billion cubic metres of gas will be delivered over the contract period. Statoil said a decision on which fields would supply the gas would be made later.

Statoil, Norsk Hydro ASA and Saga Petroleum ASA are permanent members of the GFU. During the talks with SNAM, Total Norge and Mobil Exploration Norway have also been part of the team, the statement said.

"This contract will increase Norwegian gas sales by about 10 percent," Statoil said. "Before the agreement, Norwegian suppliers had committed themselves to deliver 62 billion cubic metres of gas annually from the year 2000. This level will now increase to 68 billion cubic metres."
Norwegian gas will have a market share of 16 percent in Western Europe from the year 2000, it said.
